newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.84 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.84 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose on Thursday in selective buying which accelerated in the afternoon on news that the new year holiday was extended to five days and payments would be delayed to after the holiday, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 97,425.62, up 2,690.27 points, or 2.84 percent from Wednesday and compared to a previous record of 94,879.14 on December 20.
In dollar terms, the index stood at 91 cents, up from 89.5 cents on December 20, but down from a $1 record on April 8.
"Purchases were fuelled by afternoon news that the new year holiday was extended. It was seen positive that settlements would be delayed," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.

The goverment extended the holiday to five days by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday. The Exchange said afterwards the market would be closed on Monday and Tuesday and today's transactions would be settled on January 2, and Friday's transactions on January 3.
Brokers said delayed settlements would allow traders to place their funds in repo deals over the holiday.
Trade volume rose to 14.85 trillion lira ($138.6 million) from Thursday's 11.70 trillion ($109 million).
